title: Clothes and weather
cando: say what you are wearing and what the weather is like

about.text: This lesson is about clothes and weather. You buy a coat in a shop. You say what you are wearing.
goals: Say the weather: It's cold. It's raining.
Say your clothes: I'm wearing a coat.
Try on clothes and say: It's too big.
Read a notice about clothes at work.
Ask for a smaller size in a shop.

chapters.title: In a clothes shop
chapters.text:
This lesson is about clothes and weather.
First, Mei is in a shop. She wants a coat.
Listen for the weather. It's cold, and it's raining.
Mei asks: Can I try it on?
Then she says: It's too big.

chapters.title: The weather and your clothes
chapters.text:
For the weather, start with it. It's hot. It's cold. It's raining.
For your clothes now, say: I'm wearing. I'm wearing a hat.
Too big is a problem. Too small is a problem too.
Put on means start wearing. Take off means stop wearing.

chapters.title: A cold morning
chapters.text:
Next, you read about Tomasz. It's a cold morning.
He puts on his clothes for work.
At work, there is a notice. It says what to wear.
Then you write about your clothes today.

chapters.title: Clothes for tomorrow
chapters.text:
Then you need clothes for tomorrow. It's cold, with rain.
You go to a shop. The jumper is too big.
Say: Can I have a smaller size, please?

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story. It's about clothes and weather.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again.

warmup.prompt: It's cold outside. What do you put on?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. On a cold day, many people wear all three!

conversation.title: This coat is too big
conversation.setting: Mei is in a clothes shop. It is cold outside.
lines: Yes, please. I want a coat.
It's very cold, and it's raining.
Thank you. Can I try it on?
Yes, this is good. How much is it?
Twenty pounds. Do you want a bag?

wrong: It's cold, but it isn't raining.
questions.why: Mei says: It's very cold, and it's raining.

questions.q: What is the problem with the first coat?
questions.why: Mei tries it on and says: It's too big.

questions.q: How much is the small coat?
questions.why: The shop assistant says: Twenty pounds.

phrases.use: Saying what the weather is like.
People in shops say this to you.
Asking to put on clothes in a shop, before you buy them.
Saying the size is not right for you.
A question in a clothes shop.

items.meaning: Hot or cold? Rain or sun? That is the weather.
Not cold. You do not need a coat.
Not hot. You need a coat.
Water that falls from the sky. When it falls, we say: It's raining.
The big light in the sky. It makes the day hot.
items.example: Let's eat outside in the sun.
The wind is very cold today.

items.meaning: You wear it outside, over your clothes. It is for cold days.
items.example: Put on your coat. It's cold.

items.meaning: You wear it on your head.
You wear them on your feet.
To have clothes on your body.
items.example: I wear a white shirt at work.

items.meaning: To put on clothes in a shop. Are they right for you?
items.example: Can I try these shoes on?

items.meaning: How big or small clothes are.

sound.title: hot and hat
sound.explain: These two words are not the same. Hot has the sound in not and shop. Hat has the sound in bag and black. Listen, then say each group.
lines: It's hot. Take off your hat.

sayIt.instructions: Say Mei's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Is your voice clear?
lines: Yes, please. I want a coat.
It's very cold, and it's raining.
Thank you. Can I try it on?

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation.
spot.question: Which two are about the weather? Which one is a problem? Which one says what Mei is wearing?
spot.answer: The weather starts with it: It's cold. It's raining. Too big is a problem: the coat is not right. I'm wearing it: the coat is on Mei now.

rules.title: The weather and your clothes
rule: The weather: It is hot. It is cold. It is raining.
Clothes now: I am wearing a coat. She is wearing a hat.
A problem: It is too big. It is too small.
Put on means start wearing. Take off means stop wearing.
rules.mistake: Not: Is cold. Say: It is cold. Not: I wearing a hat. Say: I am wearing a hat.

practice.why: I am + wearing: this is now.
The weather starts with it: It is cold.
It is raining: the rain is falling now.

practice.q: This coat is too ___ . Can I have a small one?
practice.why: The coat is too big, so she wants a small one.

practice.q: My shoes are too ___ . Can I have a bigger size?
practice.why: The shoes are too small, so you want a bigger size.

practice.q: It's hot in here. ___ off your jumper.

practice.why: In a shop, you try clothes on before you buy them.

practice.q: A: What's the ___ like? B: It's hot.
practice.why: What's the weather like? asks about hot, cold, rain and sun.
Ana is one person, so she is wearing.

yourTurn.prompt: Look at your clothes now. What are you wearing? What's the weather like? Write three or four short lines.
yourTurn.model: I am wearing a blue shirt. I am wearing black trousers. It is cold today. It is raining.

text.title: A cold morning
text.type: A short text and a notice
text.body:
It is seven in the morning.
It is cold. It is raining.
Tomasz puts on a white shirt.
He puts on a jumper and trousers.
He puts on his coat and hat.
There is a notice at work.

WHAT TO WEAR HERE
Wear a white shirt.
Wear black trousers and shoes.
Do not wear a hat.
Take off your coat here.

wrong: hot, with a lot of sun
gist.why: It is cold. It is raining.
The notice says what to wear at work.

detail.why: It is seven in the morning.

detail.q: What colour is the shirt for work?
detail.why: The notice says: Wear a white shirt.

detail.q: Tomasz is wearing a hat. What does he do at work?
wrong: He puts on a new hat.
detail.why: The notice says: Do not wear a hat.

detail.q: Where does Tomasz take off his coat?
detail.why: The notice at work says: Take off your coat here.

items.meaning: All the things you wear. Shirts and coats are clothes.
Clothes for the top of your body. Many people wear one to work.
You wear them on your legs. We always say trousers, with an s.
Clothes for a woman, in one piece. Not a shirt and trousers.
It is for cold days. You wear it over a shirt.
items.example: It's cold. Put on a jumper.
Put on your coat. It's raining.

model.title: My clothes today
model.body:
Today it is hot.
I am wearing a white shirt.
I am wearing blue trousers.
I am not wearing a coat.
My shoes are black.

write.task: Write about your clothes today. Copy the model. Then change the weather, the clothes and the colours.
write.starter: Today it is … . I am wearing …
checklist: I wrote the weather: It is …
I wrote I am wearing, two or three times.
The colour comes first: a white shirt.
Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

card.title: Clothes for tomorrow
card.situation: The weather for tomorrow: cold, with rain and wind. You need a jumper. You go to a clothes shop.
card.goal: Choose your clothes for tomorrow's weather. Then try on a jumper. It is too big. Ask for a smaller size.

phrases: I want a jumper for tomorrow.
Very cold, with rain and wind.
Can I have a smaller size, please?
Yes, this is good. How much is it?
prepare.notes: Write the weather for tomorrow. Then write three clothes for tomorrow, with a colour: a blue jumper.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, say the weather for tomorrow and your clothes. Then your teacher is the shop assistant. Try on a jumper and ask for a smaller size. Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: First, ask me: What is the weather like tomorrow? What do you wear? Then be a shop assistant in a clothes shop. I try on a jumper. It is too big. Ask my size. Give me a smaller size. Use very short, simple sentences.

model.title: At the clothes shop
lines: Yes, please. I want a jumper for tomorrow.
Yes. Very cold, with rain and wind.
Thank you. Can I try it on?
It's too big. Can I have a smaller size, please?
Here you are. This is a small.
Yes, this is good. How much is it?
Sixteen pounds? OK. Here you are.
compare: Did you say the weather for tomorrow?
Did you ask: Can I try it on?
Did you say: It's too big?
Did you ask for a smaller size, with please?

canDo: I can say what the weather is like.
I can say what I am wearing.
I can try on clothes and say: It's too big.
I can read a notice about clothes at work.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. What is the weather like? What are the people wearing?
reading.talk: What do you wear on a cold day? And on a hot day? Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: A: What's the weather like? B: It's ___ .
quiz.why: It is raining: the rain is falling now.
She is wearing: she is one person.

quiz.q: The coat is too big. Can I have a ___ size, please?
quiz.why: Too big, so you want a smaller size.

quiz.q: In a shop, you want to put on a coat. What do you ask?
quiz.why: Try on: wear it in the shop to see if it is right.

quiz.q: You are inside, and it's hot. What do you do with your jumper?
What do you wear on your head?
quiz.why: A hat goes on your head.

quiz.q: My ___ are black. I wear them to work.
quiz.why: We always say trousers, so my trousers are.
The colour comes first: a red bag.

quiz.q: There ___ two bedrooms in my flat.
quiz.why: Two bedrooms is more than one, so there are.

quiz.q: I ___ hungry. Can I have a sandwich?
quiz.why: Say I am hungry, not I have hungry.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the shop conversation in pairs. Then change the clothes: shoes, a jumper, a hat. Start each one with: What's the weather like?
Day 2: the real-life task. Each learner says the weather for tomorrow and their clothes. You are the shop assistant: each learner tries on a jumper and asks for a smaller size.
Day 3: talk about the book. Then each learner says what they are wearing today, with colours.
